newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta paper mill gets agreement in principle.
newsitem.headline: Alberta paper mill gets agreement in principle.

text.p: The Alberta government said on Monday it reached an agreement with Grande Alberta Paper Ltd to allow the company to proceed with regulatory submissions for a proposed C$900 million paper mill.

Alberta said the agreement would allow Grande Alberta, which wants to build a lightweight mill at Grande Prairie, to proceed with preparing an environmental impact assessment, then be subject to a Natural Resources Conservation Board review.
The province said no government money would be provided to the project.

As part of the government decision, a forest management agreement area and timber quota of 800,000 cubic metres per year has been reserved for the proposal, it said. The annual allowable cut would be made up of 40 percent deciduous and 60 percent coniferous timber from the Grande Prairie region.
The Grande Alberta proposal includes building a single lighteight coated mill, the first high-quality paper operation in Alberta.
It would have a capacity of 350,000 scale weight short tons of paper.
